turns.doctor_question: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you into the clinic today?
turns.patient_response: Hi, thank you. Um, well, I came in today because I keep getting these really nagging thoughts. I'm a designer, and lately I just keep worrying that I’ve missed some tiny mistake in a layout, or maybe I sent the wrong version of a file to a client. And the frustrating part is, even when I check and I can see it’s probably fine, my mind just keeps circling back to it anyway. It just won't let it go.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient describes recurrent, intrusive, and nagging thoughts about making mistakes that their mind keeps circling back to.
symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient mentions checking their work in response to their nagging thoughts, indicating a checking compulsion.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from your work, do you find yourself constantly worrying about other everyday areas of your life, such as family, health, or finances?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. It's pretty much just focused on my work. I don't really worry about my health or money or anything like that more than a normal person would. It's just... the design files and the layouts. That's where I get stuck.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies worrying excessively about everyday areas of life like health or finances.

turns.doctor_question: When you have these thoughts, do you find yourself repeatedly checking your work over and over again to try to relieve the anxiety?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I do. Um, before I submit any work now, I'll usually go back and re-open the file. I'll compare the layers, re-save it, and... sometimes I just sit there and mentally walk through every single design choice one more time. It doesn't take over my whole day or anything, but it definitely makes me a lot slower. And it just makes me feel less free creatively when I'm having to do all that extra checking.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient confirms engaging in repetitive checking behaviors and mental acts (re-opening files, comparing layers, mentally walking through design choices) in response to their thoughts.

turns.doctor_question: Deep down, do you view this repetitive checking as excessive and senseless, or does it feel like a necessary way to maintain your standards?
turns.patient_response: Um, I'm not really sure, to be honest. I guess I haven't thought about it quite like that. I mean, part of me feels like it's just a way to make sure the work is perfect and maintain my standards, but... I don't know. I really couldn't say if it's completely senseless or not. I'm just not sure.

turns.doctor_question: Outside of your design work, would you say you are generally very rigid about rules, orderliness, and having things done your exact way?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. Outside of work, I'm actually pretty laid back. I mean, my house isn't perfectly spotless, and I don't really have a strict schedule or anything. I don't get upset if someone does something differently than how I'd do it at home. It's really just the design files where I get so caught up in the details.
